issues: File expo-app/src/screens/ExportScreen.tsx: The export screen never uses expo-sharing to open the native share sheet. It only shows a success message after the GET request. The spec requires saving the downloaded CSV/PDF (e.g., with expo-file-system) and calling expo-sharing's shareAsync to let the user save or send the file.

File expo-app/src/screens/ReceiptCaptureScreen.tsx: The receipt capture screen only launches ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync and does not provide a way to take a photo with the device camera. The spec requires using expo-image-picker to let the user take a photo (launchCameraAsync) or pick from the library, with proper permission handling. The current grantPermission shortcut does not request real camera permissions.

File expo-app/src/screens/ReceiptCaptureScreen.tsx: Permission handling is incomplete. The code sets hasPermission to true via a dummy function instead of calling ImagePicker.requestCameraPermissionsAsync() and handling the granted/denied status. This means the camera permission flow does not work on real devices.
feedback: The backend passes all acceptance tests and static validation, but the Expo app is missing key functionality required by the task description. Implement proper camera capture in ReceiptCaptureScreen (including permission requests) and integrate expo-sharing in ExportScreen to actually share the exported CSV/PDF files. Once these UI features are added and tested, the solution should meet the specification.
